title: How to work cross-stitch on Aida band
subtitle: Stitching a border or repeat on a pre-woven ribbon with an Aida grid
excerpt: Aida band is a narrow woven ribbon that has an Aida grid built into it with finished edges, usually in a single colour with a different-coloured border. It is used for bookmarks, belts, bag handles, and decorative borders that need a repeating cross-stitch design on a self-finishing ribbon. The ribbon already has finished edges, so no hemming or fraying is involved.
sourceNotes: Aida band cross-stitch technique. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch and embroidery publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.
The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch.

content.text: woven as a ribbon rather than fabric by the metre, with finished edges included. The grid squares are the same as standard Aida and are worked the same way, but the narrow width limits the design to a single row of squares or a short pattern repeat. Most Aida band is sold in 14-count; the stitching process is identical to stitching on Aida fabric.
Cut the Aida band to the required length, adding 3–4 cm at each end for turning under or finishing. The band's cut ends will fray if left exposed; fold them under and tack them before beginning.

Mount the band in a hoop or hold it taut in the hand. Because the band is narrow, a standard round hoop may need to be placed sideways so the band runs across the hoop diameter. Alternatively, a long slot frame is better suited to narrow work.
Find the centre of the design on the chart, and the centre of the stitching area on the band. Work outward from the centre in both directions so the design is centred within the band's length.

strand count appropriate for the band's thread count. On 14-count Aida band, 2 strands gives a standard fill. Check that the stitches lie smooth within the band's narrow width and do not pull the band into a curve.

Finish the ends of the band by folding them under by 1 cm and tacking with a running stitch in a thread that matches the band colour. The finished band should be the same width throughout with neat, even ends.

items.symptom: The band curves or bows after stitching
items.cause: Thread tension pulled the stitches unevenly across the width of the band, or the thread runs on the back are too long.
items.fix: Press the band from the back with a damp cloth. Pin it flat on a blocking board and allow it to dry. For future work, keep back thread runs shorter and ease the stitch tension slightly so the band lies flat rather than being pulled by the thread weight.

items.symptom: The stitching is off-centre on the band
items.cause: The design was started from one end rather than the centre.
items.fix: Always find the centre of the available stitching area and the centre of the design first. Mark the band centre with a pin before beginning.

content.text: A cross-stitch bookmark is a practical first Aida band project. A single repeat of a small motif centred on a 25 cm length of band, with the ends folded under and tacked, makes a complete and useful object. The project uses only a small amount of thread and takes one or two sessions.
